name: Brightline Hi-Vis Construction Shell
description:
High-visibility orange and yellow, retroreflective tape in ANSI-compliant stripes across the chest, back, and arms. The Brightline is the jacket you see on every active construction site in GLMZ — worn by the people building the elevated transit lines, maintaining the power conduit runs, and doing the physical work that keeps the megacity standing. It's a windbreaker-weight shell with a quilted vest liner that can be removed in warmer months. The fit is utilitarian and generous enough to layer over coveralls.

Brightline is a Tier 1 to 2 safety brand that sells direct to construction companies and labor cooperatives. Individual workers sometimes buy their own when site-issued jackets wear out. The jacket carries no cachet — it is purely functional — but it's an honest symbol of labor in a city that increasingly tries to make its working infrastructure invisible.
what_it_says: You work. You build things. You're not ashamed of it.
story_hooks: Someone is using stolen Brightline jackets to move through restricted construction zones undetected — and one of the real workers is being blamed.
A labor organizer has been using the hi-vis jacket as a covert signal system — specific tape patterns indicate meeting times and locations.
A Tier 5 architect was found dead in a Brightline jacket on a construction site they'd never been authorized to visit.

physical_description.visual_profile: A boldly utilitarian windbreaker with ANSI-compliant high-visibility paneling. The dominant orange-yellow colorway makes the wearer impossible to miss on any construction site or elevated platform. The silhouette is boxy and practical, designed for function over form, with a straightforward athletic cut that prioritizes safety and layering capacity over contemporary fashion.
physical_description.fit: Generous and relaxed through the torso and shoulders, with dropped armholes and a straight cut through the body. Built to accommodate heavy layering—coveralls, thermal base layers, tool belts. The sleeves are slightly oversized to allow for wrist-mounted augmentation interfaces and work gloves. Hem hits mid-hip for ease of movement.
physical_description.primary_material: Ballistic-weave nylon windbreaker shell with a quilted polyester thermal liner that detaches via reinforced seams. The liner provides insulation for cold months while the outer shell handles wind and light precipitation.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly stiff ballistic nylon on the exterior with a matte finish. Retroreflective tape has a subtle grip texture—tactile enough to catch light at any angle. The quilted liner is soft and slightly crinkly with a honeycomb pattern visible when removed.
physical_description.color_scheme: Safety orange as the primary field color with high-contrast yellow-lime secondary panels. ANSI-compliant retroreflective silver-white stripe geometry runs across the chest, back, and down both sleeves in regulation width. No logos or branding visible on the front—Brightline's name appears only on a small woven label at the interior collar.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty plastic YKK zipper with a molded pull tab large enough for gloved operation. Two-flap storm flap over the zipper. Magnetic snap pocket flaps on the chest. The liner attaches via friction-fit reinforced seams at the shoulders and sides—designed for fast removal and reattachment.
distinctive_features: Removable quilted thermal liner with its own interior zippered pockets
ANSI-compliant retroreflective tape pattern engineered for visibility in low-light conditions
Reinforced seams at stress points (shoulders, armpits, underarms)
Two deep hand-warmer pockets with water-resistant fabric backing
Interior zippered media pocket sized for a QUANTA-linked work slate
Adjustable drawcord hem and hood-less collar opening
Grommet ventilation eyelets in the side seams for heat management during active labor
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 working-class functional wear. Not luxury, but quality construction issued or purchased by organized labor. The brand carries credibility on any active site in GLMZ—it signals competence and compliance rather than status.
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of GLMZ's visible labor force. Wearing this jacket announces you are part of the infrastructure workforce—the elevated-transit builders, power-conduit maintenance crews, structural riggers, and site safety coordinators. It is a mark of honest work in a city that increasingly hides or automates away its physical labor. Worn with pride by those who build the city; occasionally worn ironically by corpo middle-managers doing site inspections.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and worn but well-maintained. Tape edges slightly lifted at the corners from repeated flexing and laundering. Minor scuffs on the lower hem from tool contact. The zipper pull may be reinforced with electrical tape or custom grip modifications. Liner shows gentle crease patterns from regular removal/reattachment. Small burn marks from welding sparks not uncommon on active construction sites.

image_prompt: A Tier 2 construction worker wearing a Brightline Hi-Vis Construction Shell stands on an elevated platform overlooking a rain-slicked GLMZ megacity district. Shot from chest-up, three-quarter angle. The orange and yellow safety jacket is crisp but realistically worn—retroreflective tape glinting under moody amber street-level lighting and cooler overhead arc lights. The worker's visible augmentation (a chrome reinforced knuckle, a glowing subcutaneous wrist-port) contrasts with the utilitarian fabric. Dark industrial background: partially constructed elevated rail infrastructure, power conduit runs, mist rising from thermal vents. Shot with a documentary photojournalism aesthetic. Cinematic, cool color grading with hot safety orange as the dominant accent. --ar 2:3 --v 6
